title: Characterization of Carbon Products Produced by Catalytic Pyrolysis of Methane
content: Catalytic pyrolysis of natural gas (NGCP), a chemical process that transforms methane (CH4) (natural gas into hydrogen and solid carbon without a CO2 byproduct [1-3], has been proposed as a near term solution for the production of hydrogen, while proposed alternative hydrogen production technologies are demonstrated and, upon being demonstrated as viable, allowed to mature. For NGCP to be successfully implemented, the generated carbon products need to be value added and aligned with target markets so that they can handle the influx of carbon products generated in combination with hydrogen. The alignment of the various generated carbon products within the targeted markets entails selectivity tailoring the properties and allotropes to maximize the value-added character of the material. In order to adapt to the various markets initially involves utilizing various separation and analytical techniques to develop methods to characterize the carbon products. [4,5]
